## Goals

- Understand the basics of Quarto.
- Create your first Quarto report by walking through a mini data project.


## Quarto Document

A template is available here:
[link](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/InforBio/ioc-r-2026/refs/heads/main/ioc_r/r_contents/week09/r_w09_example.qmd.txt). Download it and remove the suffix ".txt".

- Modify the YAML header at the top of the Quarto file:
change the `title`, `author`, or any other metadata to personalize the document.
- Write your R code directly in the Quarto document in code chunks (` ```{r}...``` `) to complete this exercise.
- Render the document (click “Render” in RStudio) to generate your first report.


## Mini Data Project

### Data Import & Exploration

1. Import the two data datasets with `read_csv()` using following links:

- Yeast gene annotation data:
`"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/InforBio/ioc-r-2026/refs/heads/main/ioc_r/r_contents/exos_data/mart_export.txt.gz"`,
  name the data as `annot`.
- Gene differential expression analysis (SET1 *vs.* WT):
`"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/InforBio/ioc-r-2026/refs/heads/main/ioc_r/r_contents/exos_data/toy_DEanalysis.csv"`, name the data as `de_res`.

What are the dimensions of each dataset?


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
library(tidyverse)
annot <- read_csv(
  "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/InforBio/ioc-r-2026/refs/heads/main/ioc_r/r_contents/exos_data/mart_export.txt.gz"
)
de_res <- read_csv(
  "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/InforBio/ioc-r-2026/refs/heads/main/ioc_r/r_contents/exos_data/toy_DEanalysis.csv"
)
```
:::

3. For protein-coding genes, calculate the maximum, minimum, average, and median percentage of GC content for each chromosome.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
annot |>
  filter(`Gene type` == "protein_coding") |>
  group_by(`Chromosome/scaffold name`) |>
  summarise(
    min_gc = min(`Gene % GC content`),
    max_gc = max(`Gene % GC content`),
    mean_gc = mean(`Gene % GC content`),
    median_gc = median(`Gene % GC content`)
```

5. Add the annotation information to `de_res`, merge the `annot` data with `de_res` using either:
- the `merge()` function (base R), or
- the `left_join()` function (from the dplyr package, `?left_join`)


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
de_res_annot <- merge(
  x = de_res, y = annot,
  by.x = "gene_name", by.y = "Gene name",
  all.x = TRUE
) # the output is no longer a tibble but data frame
de_res_annot <- as_tibble(de_res_annot) # convert to a tibble

# or with left_join
de_res_annot <- de_res |>
  left_join(annot, by = c("gene_name" = "Gene name"))
```
:::


### Data Visualization & Statistical Analysis

6. Generate a Volcano plot for differential expression results with the following specifications:

- X-axis: Log2 fold change
- Y-axis: -log10(p-value)
- Color: Highlight genes with adjusted p-values below 0.5 in red color (consider creating a new column to flag these).
- Display gene names for points with absolute log2 fold change greater than 1.5 (use `geom_text_repel()`).
- Reference lines:
  - Horizontal red dash line at the Bonferroni-adjusted p-value threshold (0.05 / Ntest)
  - Vertical dash lines at log2 fold change values of 1.5 and -1.5
- Theme: Apply `theme_light()` for the plot appearance.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
de_res_annot |>
  mutate(significant = ifelse(padj < 0.05, "yes", "no")) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = log2FoldChange, y = -log10(pvalue))) +
  geom_point(aes(color = significant), alpha = 0.7) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("yes" = "red", "no" = "grey")) +
  labs(color = "adj.p < 0.05") +
  ggrepel::geom_text_repel(
    data = filter(de_res_annot, abs(log2FoldChange) > 1.5),
    aes(label = gene_name) # use gene name as lable
  ) +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = -log10(0.05 / nrow(de_res_annot)),
    color = "red",
    linetype = "dashed" 
  ) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(1.5, -1.5), linetype = "dashed") +
  theme_light()
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](r_w09_exos_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-6-1.png){width=672}
:::

```{.r .cell-code}
# or without create new column for colors
de_res_annot |>
  ggplot(aes(x = log2FoldChange, y = -log10(pvalue))) +
  geom_point(aes(color = padj < 0.05), alpha = 0.7) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("TRUE" = "red", "FALSE" = "grey")) +
  labs(color = "adj.p < 0.05") +
  ggrepel::geom_text_repel(
    data = filter(de_res_annot, abs(log2FoldChange) > 1.5),

  ) +
```

So far, we've analyzed gene expression between two groups (SET1 *vs.* WT).
How can we compare expression levels across four groups (WT, SET1, SET1.RRP6, RRP6)?
For example, how can we test if the average expression level of a gene is the same across these four groups?

:::{.callout-tip title="Stats Time!"}
**One-way ANOVA**

ANOVA (**AN**alysis **O**f **VA**riance) helps us determine whether the means of multiple groups are different. Instead of comparing means directly (as in t-tests),
ANOVA compares the variances within (intra) and between groups (inter) to infer differences in means.

We assume that the variance within each group is the same across all groups.

![](images/anova_img.png){width=80%}

(Figure credit: Lorette Noiret)

- $H_0: \mu_1 = \mu_2 = ... = \mu_n$
- $H_1$: there is at least one group which has an average different than other groups.

Which is equals to test:

- $H_0: \sigma^2_{\text{inter group}} = \sigma^2_{\text{intra group}}$
- $H_1: \sigma^2_{\text{inter group}} > \sigma^2_{\text{intra group}}$

If the means are truly different, the variation between groups ($\sigma^2_{\text{inter group}}$) should be greater than the variation within groups ($\sigma^2_{\text{intra group}}$).

ANOVA calculates the F statistic, which is a ratio:

$F = \frac{\sigma^2_{\text{inter group}}}{\sigma^2_{\text{intra group}}}$

, and the probability of obtaining an F-statistic as extreme as the observed one (the p-value), assuming the null hypothesis is true.

Conditions of applying ANOVA:

- Independence: Observations in each group must be independent.
- Normality: Data should be approximately normally distributed (can be checked using the Shapiro test).
- Homoscedasticity (homogeneity of variance): Variances across groups should be roughly equal (Levene’s test or Bartlett’s test can check this).

In R, the function `aov()` is used to perform ANOVA.
::: 

Let's take the gene *LOH1* as example.

7. Import the expression data using this link:
`"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/InforBio/ioc-r-2026/refs/heads/main/ioc_r/r_contents/exos_data/read-counts.csv"`


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
counts <- read_csv(
  "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/InforBio/ioc-r-2026/refs/heads/main/ioc_r/r_contents/exos_data/read-counts.csv"
)
```
:::



8. Given the imported counts data, how can we reshape it to extract the necessary information and obtain a tibble with the following columns?

- "value": Expression values of the gene *LOH1*
- "group": Sample groups (Explore how to use the `str_replace()` function to extract group based on sample name)


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
anova_data <- counts |>
  filter(Feature == "LOH1") |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -1,
    names_to = "sample_id",
    values_to = "value"
  ) |>
  mutate(group = sub("(.*)\\.([0-9]+)", "\\1", sample_id)) # use regular expression
anova_data
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```

# ℹ 30 more rows
```


:::
:::


9. Assume that all conditions of ANOVA are verified.
Perform an ANOVA (`aov()`) test and use `summary()` to obtain the results.
If we take $\alpha=0.05$, what is your conclusion?


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
res_aov <- aov(value ~ group, data = anova_data)
summary(res_aov)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
            Df Sum Sq Mean Sq F value  Pr(>F)    
group        3  45166   15055   13.69 4.1e-06 ***
Residuals   36  39603    1100                    
---
Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
```


:::
:::


10. Conduct a Tukey Honest Significant Differences (TukeyHSD) test to check which groups differ significantly. (`?TukeyHSD`)


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
TukeyHSD(res_aov)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```

WT-SET1        -93.3 -133.24833 -53.351674 0.0000017
WT-SET1.RRP6   -38.9  -78.84833   1.048326 0.0587008
```


:::
:::


11. Visualize the expression levels of the *LOH1* gene across the four groups using a boxplot. Comment on the figure.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
ggplot(
  anova_data,
  aes(
    x = factor(group, levels = c("WT", "SET1", "SET1.RRP6", "RRP6")),
    y = value
  )
) +
  geom_boxplot(
    outliers = FALSE # do not display outliers by boxplot
  ) +
  geom_point(
    aes(color = group),
    position = position_jitter(height = 0, width = 0.3, seed = 1)
  ) +
  labs(x = NULL, title = "Expression of LOH1") +
  theme_light() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](r_w09_exos_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-11-1.png){width=672}

### Bonus

Verify the assumptions for conducting an ANOVA test:


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# Check data normality with Shapiro test
shapiro.test(anova_data$value[anova_data$group == "WT"])
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```

	Shapiro-Wilk normality test

data:  anova_data$value[anova_data$group == "WT"]
W = 0.92104, p-value = 0.3657
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
shapiro.test(anova_data$value[anova_data$group == "SET1"])
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```

	Shapiro-Wilk normality test

data:  anova_data$value[anova_data$group == "SET1"]
W = 0.90683, p-value = 0.2599
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
shapiro.test(anova_data$value[anova_data$group == "SET1.RRP6"])
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```

	Shapiro-Wilk normality test

data:  anova_data$value[anova_data$group == "SET1.RRP6"]
W = 0.92342, p-value = 0.3864
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
shapiro.test(anova_data$value[anova_data$group == "RRP6"])
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```

	Shapiro-Wilk normality test

data:  anova_data$value[anova_data$group == "RRP6"]
W = 0.81775, p-value = 0.02381
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
# or use lapply() to repeat test for each group
# lapply(
#   X = unique(anova_data$group),
#   FUN = function(grp) {
#     shapiro.test(anova_data$value[anova_data$group == grp])
#   }
# )
```
:::


The RRP6 data does not follow a normal distribution.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# Check homogeneity of variance with Bartlett test
bartlett.test(value ~ group, data = anova_data)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```

	Bartlett test of homogeneity of variances

data:  value by group
Bartlett's K-squared = 25.242, df = 3, p-value = 1.374e-05
```


:::
:::


Moreover, the assumption of homoscedasticity (equal variance) is not met.

Therefore, an ANOVA is not appropriate, and a non-parametric Kruskal-Wallis test should be used instead.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
kruskal.test(value ~ group, data = anova_data)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```

	Kruskal-Wallis rank sum test

data:  value by group
Kruskal-Wallis chi-squared = 24.631, df = 3, p-value = 1.845e-05
```


:::
:::
